title: Why on earth is Sara’s team playing videos of departed people for her defense?
summary: 'They are exploiting the dead,' one prosecutor says of the defense team after it played videos of Renato Corona and Miriam Santiago in Sara Duterte's trial

blocks.text: 'They are exploiting the dead,' one prosecutor says of the defense team after it played videos of Renato Corona and Miriam Santiago in Sara Duterte's trial

items: During the impeachment court session on November 19, Vice President Sara Duterte's legal counsel controversially played videos of deceased figures Renato Corona and Miriam Defensor Santiago as part of the defense strategy.
Senators expressed confusion and concern over the relevance of the videos, questioning why the defense was using footage of the deceased in the trial.

It was an unusual Thursday morning, November 19, at the impeachment court when the legal counsel of Vice President Sara Duterte spent so much time playing videos of the late chief justice Renato Corona and the late senator Miriam Defensor Santiago as part of her defense strategy.
“Weird,” private prosecutor Amando Virgil Ligutan quipped.
Why exploit the dead?
Defense lawyer Mark Vinluan first showed a video of Santiago’s interjection during Corona’s trial in 2012, in which she berated the prosecution and accused it of conducting a trial by publicity.
“What is the relevance of all this? We’re like watching a movie,” Senator Erwin Tulfo said. “Let us allow the departed to rest in peace.”

“I don’t see the significance of the opinion of one of the 24 senator-judges in the trial of the late chief justice Renato Corona,” Senator Ping Lacson added. In the 2012 trial, Santiago was one of only three senators who voted to acquit the magistrate on charges stemming from untruthful disclosure of his net worth.

blocks.caption: Why on earth is Sara’s team playing videos of departed people for her defense?

blocks.text: Vinluan just moved on to his next point. Later, he spent more than 10 minutes playing a portion of the nearly three-hour long testimony of Corona in his 2012 trial, specifically the part in which he was crying.
The video was a setup to Vinluan’s question on persecution.
“What is the effect of weaponizing the (Anti-Money Laundering Council) against any individual or his or her family in terms of financial investigation?” Vinluan asked its witness.
Prosecutor Chel Diokno objected to the question, which he said was irrelevant, immaterial and misleading. Presiding officer Chiz Escudero nonetheless overruled the objection.
The prosecution was perplexed by the defense’s strategy to show videos of the dead.
“The defense is bringing back the dead to defend the Vice President,” Ligutan said on the sidelines of the trial. “They are clutching at straws.”
“They are reviving the dead. They are exploiting the dead,” he added.
Prosecutor Terry Ridon shared similar sentiments.
“I think they cannot find a living witness today,” Ridon quipped. “This is more of like a crying tactic for the fans.”

“I think the Senate impeachment court should have more control on the videos that are being presented because I think it is clear as day that if the video presentation has no relation to the (matter at hand), why show it?” he argued.
For the record, the videos were played while the defense was conducting its direct examination of CPA lawyer and “anti-money laundering expert” Rainer dela Fuente.
Alas, his morning testimony was rather forgettable. – Rappler.com
